title: Batch-slot + latency-slab pricing pilot for embeddings & rerank
creator: Sana Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood has several parallel efforts to change how we price embeddings and reranking so we better align unit economics to customer workloads. Current feedback from mid-market customers: (1) per-vector pricing is easy to reason about but punishes bursty/mini-batch workloads, (2) large customers want predictable spend when they bundle many short vectors in a single request, and (3) some customers are willing to pay a premium for guaranteed low-latency (sub-100ms) routing.

Goal:
Run a controlled pilot that tests two new levers: 1) 'Batch slots' — a committed / on-demand per-request discount that scales with per-request aggregation size, and 2) 'Latency slabs' — optional premium surcharge for requests routed to priority low-latency pools. Evaluate impacts on revenue per vector, average price paid per logical query, churn risk, and QSA/contract surface.

Proposal (pilot design):
- Pricing primitives:
  • Base per-vector price (public): $0.0008 / vector (no batching).
  • Batch-slot discount tiers (applied when multiple vectors are submitted in the same request):
    - 1-8 vectors: no discount (base)
    - 9-64 vectors: 15% discount per vector
    - 65-256 vectors: 30% discount per vector
    - 257+ vectors: 45% discount per vector
  • Latency slabs (optional per-tenant setting):
    - Standard (default): no surcharge, routed to cost-optimized pools
    - Priority: +20% per-vector surcharge, routed to pre-warmed low-latency GPU pools (SLO: p95 < 100ms for typical vector length)
- Rerank complexity adjustment:
  • For reranking flows that require cross-encoder scoring (embedding + cross-encoder), bill an extra complexity multiplier based on top-K processed: e.g., top-5: x1.2, top-20: x1.6, top-100: x2.2. This is intended to capture CPU/GPU cross-encoder cost and KV cache pressure.
- Bundled commits / reservations:
  • Pilot supports an optional monthly reserved 'batch-slot' seat for high-volume customers (committed throughput units) which converts per-vector price into lower committed price tiers (negotiated). Demonstration offering: commit 1M batch-slot vectors/month -> 35% effective discount compared to on-demand.

Experiment cohorts and measurement:
- Cohorts (12-week pilot):
  1) New accounts (A/B): 50% see base pricing; 50% see batch-slot + latency slab options surfaced in console + API parameter (opt-in).
  2) Existing customers with >$5k/mo embedding spend: rollout via sales pilot (sales-managed negotiation).
- Primary metrics:
  • Effective $/vector (median + mean) by cohort
  • Revenue delta vs baseline for cohort (week-over-week and cumulative)
  • Average vectors per request (to measure induced batching behavior)
  • Latency SLO compliance for Priority slab (p95 latency)
  • Churn/attrition signal and NPS/text feedback from pilot customers
- Secondary metrics:
  • Billing system error rate for per-request batch accounting
  • Console conversion: percent of customers enabling latency slab or purchasing reservation

Technical and operational requirements:
- Billing / Invoicing: support for per-request aggregation detection and mapping to discount tier; table-based pricing engine changes (ENG task).
- API: new optional parameter batch_mode and priority_slab boolean to opt into behaviors; backward-compatible defaults required.
- Console UX: new Pricing -> Embeddings panel to preview effective pricing given sample payloads and to enable latency slab opt-in. Design to provide an 'Estimate cost for X vectors' widget.
- Instrumentation: dashboards for effective $/vector, request-level batch sizes, priority slab routing volume, and rerank complexity multiplier billing.
- Contracts/QSA: update standard MSA and price sheets to include Batch-slot pricing table and latency slab terms; QSA to validate no new data-sharing implications (we're not sharing customer vectors). Also add a short buyer-facing FAQ on what 'Priority' routing means for SLA and data residency.

Acceptance criteria:
- Production billing calculates discounts correctly for 100% of sampled requests over a 48h smoke window (zero mis-bills).
- Console shows accurate estimate within 5% of measured invoice for sample payloads in staging.
- Priority slab routing achieves p95 latency target in controlled test cluster for a representative payload distribution.
- Legal and Security confirm additions to pricing docs and QSA FAQ are complete; sales enablement materials created.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: customers may intentionally split requests to avoid moving into higher batch tiers (gaming). Mitigation: define time-window aggregation rules (we consider vectors in same request only; do not aggregate across separate HTTP requests) and telemetry to detect deliberate splitting patterns; consider safety-adjusted floor pricing.
- Risk: billing complexity increases ops burden. Mitigation: limit pilot to small cohort and provide clear dashboards; ensure billing rollback path (feature flag and audit log).
- Risk: latency slab causes resource contention. Mitigation: strict capacity guardrails and circuit-breaker to fallback to standard routing with customer notification.

Stakeholders and owners:
- PM (owner): Sana Patel
- Engineering owner: Diego Morales (runtime/billing coordination)
- Design: Priya Natarajan (console UX)
- Legal/QSA: Mara Chen
- Sales/Customer Success pilot: Luke Kwan

Next steps (short-term):
1) Align with Eng on data model and billing changes (ENG ticket + estimate).
2) Design console mockups and API schema (design review scheduled 2025-06-12).
3) Draft QSA and contract language, run through Legal by 2025-06-20.
4) Prepare pilot list and sales outreach for 5 initial customers.

Notes:
- This pilot is intentionally conservative on discount depth and has strong opt-in for Priority. If pilot shows customers primarily choose Priority to avoid latency variability, we'll iterate on price point and consider including a soft pre-warm credit in reserved plans.

acceptance_criteria: All billing calculations pass smoke tests; console cost estimator matches staging invoices within 5%; priority slab meets p95 latency SLO in test cluster; legal/QSA language approved and sales enablement created.
risks: Customers gaming batch sizes, operational billing complexity, priority pool contention. Mitigations: per-request aggregation rule, limited pilot cohort, capacity guardrails and fallbacks.
